STL Editor 2.0 is the same editor, rebuilt from the ground up. The tabs, panels and shortcuts are where you left them, and your projects open as they are. What changed is underneath: it is one small program, it is much faster, and the same app now runs on Windows, Mac, Linux and in the browser.

## The big changes

- **One small file.** The Windows download is a single `.exe` of about 40 MB, less than half the size of the 1.x zip. No zip to unpack, nothing to install.
- **Much faster.** On the same test parts, Hollow went from 57 s to 1.4 s, Repair › Rebuild from 11.3 s to 1.3 s, Remesh from 10 s to 2.4 s, and opening a file from 1.6 s to 0.6 s. No tool is slower than in 1.x. The 3D view is drawn by your graphics card, so big meshes stay smooth.
- **A Mac download, for the first time.** Mac and Linux get the same app as Windows. Both are beta: newer and less tested.
- **Your projects come with you.** `.stlx` projects from 1.x open and rebuild the same in 2.0.
- **Cancel a long job.** The "working" note has a Cancel button. It stops the rebuild and leaves your project as it was.

## New in the tools

- **Split connectors.** A new *Dovetail* connector slides the two halves together so they can't pull apart, and prints without supports. *How many* sets the number of connectors, and *Place by hand* lets you click where each one goes. When a cut goes through separate parts of a model, each piece can become its own body. Fit to Bed has the dovetail and *How many* too.
- **Split and Section View.** Pick any plane or flat face, then drag an arrow or type a distance to move the cut. Section View draws the cut face with hatch lines.
- **Thread: Screw head.** A tapped hole can have a pocket for a socket head cap screw or a countersunk screw. Pick the screw size and the pocket is sized for you.
- **Hole and Thread: place from an edge.** Type how far a hole is from one or two edges of the part. If the part changes size later, the hole keeps its distances.
- **Hole and Thread: move a placed point.** Drag its dot along the face instead of clearing it and clicking again.
- **Move** snaps to the grid and to the plate. Hold Shift to move freely.
- **Shell and Hollow** give a wall of exactly the thickness you set, with square inside corners.
- **Measure** also shows the distance along X, Y and Z.
- **Export STEP** is now in the desktop app as well as the web edition.
- **Send to Slicer** sends a 3MF instead of an STL, and lists only the slicers you have.

## Sketching

- **Sizes go in boxes beside the shape** as you draw, and the rest of the shape keeps following the pointer.
- **Clearer snaps.** A small marker and a word show what the pointer snapped to. A line can snap tangent to a circle or arc.
- **New colours.** The shape you are drawing is green, and closed shapes are filled pale blue.
- **A sketch on a face follows the part** when you later move, rotate or mirror it.

## Support Fins

- **Fins follow their part.** Fins kept as a separate body move with the part, and when you split it, each fin goes with the half it stands under.
- **Fins are rebuilt after you change the part.** Move, scale, lay flat or split a part that has Support Fins and the fins are made again for the part as it is now.

## Things that work differently

- **The mouse buttons changed.** Right-drag (or Shift + middle-drag) orbits, middle-drag pans, and the wheel zooms toward the part under the cursor. The left button no longer moves the view, so a stray drag can't spin the part while you pick. *View › Orbit Around* chooses what the view turns around.
- **Snap-fit is not in 2.0.** Projects that already have a Snap-fit step still open and rebuild.
- **Settings start fresh.** 2.0 keeps its own settings and recent files, apart from 1.x's, so the two can sit side by side.
- **Hand-drawn walls inside a Support Fins step** are taken out when the fins are rebuilt after a move or split. A note tells you; draw them again afterwards.
- **A new icon:** a cube with a corner cut away.

## Getting 2.0

- **Windows:** download **STL-Editor-2-Windows.exe**, put it anywhere and double-click it. It isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info › Run anyway**.
- **Mac (beta):** download **STL-Editor-2-macOS.app.zip** and unzip it. The app isn't signed by Apple, so the first time, right-click it and choose **Open**.
- **Linux (beta):** download **STL-Editor-2-x86_64.AppImage**, make it executable and run it.
- **In your browser:** https://natterman12.github.io/STL-Editor/app/ After the first visit it works with no connection. In Chrome and Edge, Save writes straight back to your project file and you can install it as an app from the address bar.
- **1.x stays as it is.** Your installed 1.x is not replaced and will not update itself to 2.0. Keep it for as long as you like. The 1.x web edition has moved to https://natterman12.github.io/STL-Editor/app1/
- **Later 2.0 updates:** the app tells you when there is a new version. On Windows, **Update now** downloads it, checks it and restarts.

## Notes

- A project saved in 2.0 that uses something new (a dovetail, a screw head pocket, a hole placed from an edge) may not rebuild the same if you open it in 1.x.
- Send to Slicer and To STEP need the desktop app. To STEP is Windows only.
- The full list of what works differently is in the user guide, under *What's different in 2.0*.
